arguments.summary: A spear-phishing campaign attributed to APT-41 (Double Dragon) successfully compromised a high-criticality finance workstation (WS-FIN-042) via malicious Outlook macro execution. The initial payload, 'chrome_helper.exe', was delivered as a weaponized attachment and executed PowerShell to deploy a ShadowPad variant using process hollowing and DLL sideloading via rundll32.exe. The malware established C2 communication over HTTPS to a known-bad IP (198.51.100.23) and a dynamic DNS domain (update.ns3.ezdns.cc), exhibiting beaconing behavior. Post-compromise activities included host file modification, SMB-based lateral movement attempts, and privilege escalation reconnaissance. The threat actor leveraged encoded PowerShell and living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins), evading initial EDR detection. Incident response actions were hindered by incorrect targeting during containment attempts.

title: Suspicious PowerShell Execution from Outlook
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
  event_id: 4688
condition:
  - CommandLine|contains: 'powershell.exe'
  - ParentProcessName|endswith: '\outlook.exe'
  - CommandLine|contains: '-enc'
  - CommandLine|contains: 'rundll32'
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate admin scripts launched from email (rare)
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566.001/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218.011/

rule ShadowPad_APT41_2026 {
    meta:
        description = "Detects ShadowPad variant used by APT-41 in 2026 campaigns"
        author = "SOC Threat Intel"
        malware_family = "ShadowPad"
        threat_actor = "APT-41"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $mutex = "Global\\APT41_ShadowPad_2026" fullword ascii
        $c2_domain = "update.ns3.ezdns.cc" fullword ascii
        $pbd_chinese = "\\\\??\\C:\\Users\\.*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\.*\\.dll" wide
    condition:
        $mutex and $c2_domain
}
